title: Aaryatech Behavioral Mechanism
description: Structural definition for one entry in behavioral_mechanisms.json. A mechanism explains WHY a consumer behavior may occur. It must NOT contain behavioral outcomes/signals, emotions, contextual triggers, or marketing/branding recommendations — those belong to separate future libraries and modules.

Pattern_ID.description: Unique ID for this mechanism. 'BM' prefix distinguishes this library from future outcome (BO-), emotion (EM-), and context (CX-) libraries.

Behavioral_Mechanism.description: The causal explanation of why this mechanism produces the described effect.

Possible_Linguistic_Signals.description: Illustrative example phrasings only. NOT a classification rule — comment-to-pattern mapping is a future module.

Possible_Contradictory_Signals.description: Example phrasings that would argue AGAINST this mechanism being present, to prevent overconfident pattern-matching later.

Related_Patterns.description: Pattern_IDs of other mechanisms this one is commonly confused with or co-occurs with. May be empty.

Distinguishing_Features.description: Required explanation of how this mechanism differs from its nearest neighbor(s). This is the anti-duplication mechanism for the library.

Evidence_Requirements.description: What kind of evidence a future module would need to reasonably infer this mechanism, rather than merely guess it.

Confidence_Notes.description: Caveats about how easily this mechanism can be confused with others or misapplied.

Source_References.description: Academic/authoritative citations, or the literal string 'SOURCE_REVIEW_REQUIRED' if a source could not be confidently verified.

Version.description: Version of this individual entry, e.g. '1.0'.
